subject: FlowRunner — Redwood adapter & tracing readiness
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@catalystai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Rivers <trivers@catalystai.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro — FlowRunner SDK + Redwood adapter interest

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — I lead partnerships at Catalyst AI. We build FlowRunner, a developer SDK for productionizing LLM pipelines (prompt orchestration, retrievers via LlamaIndex, LangChain integrations, and built-in tracing). Several joint customers asked if FlowRunner could ship a Redwood adapter for native tracing and a prebuilt connector to Redwood’s hosted and dedicated runtimes.

High level ask: can Redwood partner with us to (1) define an initial adapter that implements Redwood trace hook ingestion and LangChain/LlamaIndex helpers, (2) validate it in your sandbox, and (3) co-publish a reference implementation and docs. We think this helps drive adoption for both sides.

I attached a short API brief and sandbox-access stub. Tom (cc’d) is our engineering lead and will handle technical follow-ups.

Would love to set a short call to align on scope and timeline this week. Proposed slots: Wed 10–11 PT or Thu 2–3 PT.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto | Head of Partnerships | Catalyst AI
Attachments: FlowRunner-API-brief.pdf, integration-sandbox-access.txt
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena@catalystai.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <trivers@catalystai.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro — FlowRunner SDK + Redwood adapter interest

Elena — really appreciate the intro and context. This is squarely in our ISV partnerships lane and sounds promising. We’ve seen multiple LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations request tighter tracing and an adapter reduces onboarding friction.

I’m looping in Kimberly (Partner Engineer) and Mateo (Solutions) to scope the technical acceptance criteria and infra needs.

Quick answers and next steps:
- Wed 10–11 PT works for me; I’ll book the slot if that works for your team.
- Can you share a short mutual action plan (M.A.P) with milestone dates? We typically aim for a 6-week MVP: adapter + docs + sandbox validation.
- Important for us: trace format (schema), auth for ingestion, and data retention / PII handling for traces when used against private deployments.

Thanks — will bring a draft M.A.P to the call.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena@catalystai.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@catalystai.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro — FlowRunner SDK + Redwood adapter interest (technical Qs)

Elena / Tom — thanks for pursuing this. A few technical questions ahead of Wed so we can make the call productive: 
1) Trace schema: do you emit a single trace per request with separate event types (prompt, call, retriever, embed) or separate traces per stage? We prefer a compact JSON line schema we can ingest into our tracing pipeline.
2) Auth: will FlowRunner push traces to an endpoint (push model) or export to an S3-like store we ingest? If push, what auth (Bearer token / mTLS)?
3) PII/data residency: we need a statement for customers using Private (VPC) deployments — will FlowRunner respect on-prem tracing endpoints or forward to Catalyst-managed endpoints?
4) Open-source license for the adapter: do you plan to release under Apache-2.0 / MIT?

If you can drop a trace-schema file and a short MVP scope doc ahead of the call that would be ideal. I attached a simple suggested schema (trace-schema-v1.json) for reference to speed alignment.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park | Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: trace-schema-v1.json
From: Elena Soto <elena@catalystai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Rivers <trivers@catalystai.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro — FlowRunner SDK + Redwood adapter interest (answers + repo)

Thanks Kimberly — quick answers inline and a repo link: https://github.com/catalystai/flowrunner-redwood-adapter

1) Schema: FlowRunner emits a single trace per pipeline invocation with an events array (prompt, tool_call, retriever_call, embed). We can output either ndjson lines or a single JSON object; we’ll add a ndjson export mode.
2) Auth: primary plan is push model over HTTPS with Bearer token. For private deployments we can support mTLS if needed.
3) PII/residency: by default traces are customer-owned and can be exported to customer-managed endpoints (you’ll see sandbox-access in the attachment). We do not retain traces in Catalyst production for customers that opt-out.
4) License: we propose Apache-2.0 for the adapter and example.

Attached is a short MVP scope and a link to our repo with an initial adapter skeleton and tests. We’d like Redwood to validate ingestion on hosted + dedicated and sign off on the reference docs.

Proposed MVP milestones in the attached mvp-scope.md:
- Week 1: Align schema and auth, repo skeleton merged
- Week 2–3: Adapter implementation + unit tests (FlowRunner side)
- Week 4: Redwood sandbox validation + perf sanity checks
- Week 5: Docs, example LangChain/LlamaIndex recipes
- Week 6: Publish reference adapter + joint blog/announce

We’re open to tightening timelines. Confirming Wed 10am PT for the call — Tom and I will join.

Best,
Elena
Attachments: mvp-scope.md
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Next steps (action owners + dates):

- Redwood: run sandbox ingestion validation and provide test token by Tue 2026-01-13 (Kimberly)
- Joint: demo run and perf sanity on Wed 2026-01-20; publish draft docs by Fri 2026-01-30

I’ll create a calendar invite for the 2026-01-20 demo and share the MAP spreadsheet. Please confirm the PR date and I’ll mark tasks in our partner tracking board.

Thanks — excited to get this live.

—Vanessa
